title: Momentum Run Manifest
description: Durable state for one autonomous run, at <repo>/.momentum/run.json. The resume point: agents are stateless across turns, so everything the governor needs to restart a run after compaction, session death, or a machine restart lives here. Tier-agnostic by construction (ADR-0003's one-engine principle applied to execution) — the governor advances a cursor and never interprets what a unit means. All writes go through core/run/lib/manifest.js. Versioned from the first commit because an unversioned resume format is a migration trap.

schema_version.description: Run manifest schema version. Readers MUST tolerate unknown sibling fields (forward compatibility) but MUST refuse an unknown schema_version rather than guess.

run_id.description: Opaque short identifier (run_<hex>). Appears in park records and audit entries so artifacts can be tied back to the run that produced them.

tier.description: Which scale this run walks. The governor treats all four identically — this field exists for the CLI's rendering and for the caller that resolves a cursor into work, never for the decision function.

target.description: What is being run, at the granularity of `tier`: a group id, a phase directory name, an epic slug, or an initiative slug.

status.description: running = the governor may continue. parked = blocked on operator input past the threshold. stopped = halted by kill switch, budget, or strikes. complete/failed = terminal. Only `running` permits a `continue` decision (governor branch 1).

policy.description: The operator's standing choices for this run, resolved from specs/config.md at start and frozen for the run's lifetime. Frozen deliberately: a policy that shifts mid-run makes the audit trail unreadable.

release.description: When merge + tag happen. per-feature defers both to the end of the whole run — the epic's phases stack as lanes and land parent-first (Rule 6 Landing Order). Never finer-grained than the merge granularity it implies; enforced by `momentum config validate`.

push.description: Backup cadence. There is no `never` — an autonomous run holding multiple phases of work only in a local worktree is one crash from total loss. This is a floor rule, not a preference.

tdd.description: strict = a task cannot be marked done without a recorded red→green transition. Required whenever release is per-feature: with the human absent across several phases, the failing-then-passing test is the only evidence of progress that is not the agent's own opinion.

authority_overrides.description: Project-specific additions to the Rule-14 trigger set (ADR-0019). Widen-only: overrides may claim MORE decisions for the operator, never fewer. The invariant floor (trust-layer paths, specs/architecture/, public contracts) is not reachable from here.

park_threshold.description: How many parked decisions may accumulate before the run stops cleanly instead of limping on. Guards the pre-mortem's half-built-feature failure: returning to a 60%-complete feature across three branches is worse than returning to a clean stop.

budget.description: Bounds on an unattended run. Absent means unbounded, which is only sane for tier=group. Governor branch 3.

tokens.description: Maximum cumulative tokens, when the host reports them.

spent.description: Running totals compared against `budget`. Written by the manifest layer on each continuation.

cursor.description: Where the run is. The single source of truth for what starts next, and the idempotence guard: a backend firing onTurnEnd twice for one logical turn must not advance it twice.

unit.description: Opaque unit id, meaningful to the caller that resolves it into work — never parsed by the governor.

path.description: Ancestry from the run target down to the unit, e.g. ['phase-32a-governor','G3']. Rendering and audit only.

decisions.description: Decisions the agent took under its own authority (ADR-0019). Append-only. Each records the trigger evaluation that produced the classification, so 'why did it decide that alone?' stays answerable long after the run.

authority.description: Only agent-authority decisions land here. Operator-authority ones are parked, not decided.

triggers_evaluated.description: Which Rule-14 triggers were checked and did not fire. The negative evidence is the interesting part.

parked.description: Questions awaiting the operator. Non-blocking by construction: a parked item freezes only the thread that needs it while independent work continues. Backed by core/run/lib/inbox.js.

blocked_unit.description: The unit that cannot proceed. Other units are unaffected.

reason.description: operator-authority = a Rule-14 trigger fired. ambiguous = nothing matched and the default parked rather than guessing (ADR-0019 §4).

strikes.description: Per-unit consecutive failure counts, keyed by unit id. Reset on success. Governor branch 4 — repeated failure on one task is not progress, and retrying forever burns budget to produce noise.

amendments.description: Operator changes injected into a live run (Epic 0001 D11). forward-only amendments are absorbed silently and become inputs to the derivation of not-yet-started units; backward-invalidating ones set status=stopped and name the affected completed work. Reserved here in 32a; written by 32b.

kind.description: unclassified is treated as backward-invalidating — the safe direction when the agent cannot tell.

invalidates.description: Completed units this amendment calls into question.

grant.description: Scoped authorization covering N landings for ONE epic (ADR-0020). Offered ALONGSIDE the single-use merge-approved sentinel, never replacing it — a repo that never mints one behaves byte-identically to v0.42.0. Bounded on three axes because the honest cost of a grant is that one approval now covers code the operator has not read: scope (a branch allowlist it cannot exceed), time (a hard, non-sliding expiry), and count (a landing budget). Every consumption is audited before the push proceeds.

epic.description: The epic slug this grant is bound to. A run for any other epic is refused with `epic-mismatch`.

branches.description: The ONLY branches this grant may land. A push to anything else falls through to the sentinel path as though no grant existed — the grant cannot authorize work outside the plan's own branches.

expires.description: Absolute, never sliding. An authorization that outlives the operator's attention is the hazard most likely to bite: a run that goes wrong at hour three would otherwise still hold hour zero's yes.

landings_remaining.description: Decremented per consumption. Defaults to the epic's phase count, so a grant cannot fund landings the plan never described. Zero is `exhausted`, not unlimited.

revoked.description: Revocation takes effect on the next verification — there is no cached decision.

consumptions.description: Attributed record of every landing this grant funded. This is the compensating control for the operator no longer being present at each protected write, so it is written BEFORE the push proceeds, not after.

audit.description: Append-only event log. Every state transition the governor causes, attributed and timestamped.

red_green.description: Per-unit list of tasks with a recorded failing→passing transition (D12). Under `tdd: strict` a task cannot be marked done without an entry here. Stored rather than inferred from test output because a run must be able to prove it after the fact, from disk, with no test runner available.
